key_insight: A bead-space Cayley propagator removes Fourier transforms from RPMD spring integration while exactly reproducing the normal-mode Cayley map at linear cost.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate low-temperature molecular reaction simulations that require many ring-polymer beads without sacrificing free ring-polymer energy conservation.
method: Replace mode-by-mode propagation with one cyclic tridiagonal midpoint solve using a mass-independent matrix.
Apply Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction in about 18P operations per degree of freedom.
Implement the propagator in the open-source PyRPMD package.
evidence_signal: Tests reproduce normal-mode Cayley to 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ for up to 2048 beads, show linear cost scaling, and indicate 23–29-fold higher timestep stability limits in published low-temperature dRPMD settings.
watch_item: Stability still requires ΩΔt < 2 for the highest physical frequency, and low-lying internal modes associated with spurious resonances remain essentially unchanged.
paper_title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
